title: Composable event middleware + resumable chunk assembler for Python chat streaming
creator: Liam Chen
description: Problem: Consumers of the Python SDK currently stitch together streaming chat events manually which leads to duplicated logic, incorrect resumptions after transient network failures, and brittle retry handling for partial/incremental deltas. We need a reusable, composable middleware layer that: (1) normalizes server event frames into typed events, (2) exposes a backpressure-aware async iterator with an opt-in resumable chunk assembler for partial token/delta sequences, and (3) integrates with the SDK retry/backoff policy so applications can resume streams cleanly after transient errors.
acceptance_criteria: Provide a middleware API that can be composed (wrap/stack) around an async stream source in the Python SDK
Implement a ResumableChunkAssembler that buffers incomplete deltas across reconnects and exposes a deterministic resume token to be sent to the service
Expose a BackpressureAsyncIterator that yields high-level Event objects (MessageDelta, RoleChange, FunctionCall, Done, Error) and supports async .pause()/.resume() semantics
Integrate with existing SDK retry mechanism so stream reconnects use the assembler's resume token and respect exponential backoff + jitter
Add unit and integration tests simulating network drops, out-of-order partial frames, and duplicate replay to validate idempotence
Document middleware usage with two examples: (a) simple chat consumer that prints incremental tokens, (b) tool-calling consumer that reconstructs function call arguments after reconnect
implementation_notes: Add new module: redwood_sdk.streaming.middleware with classes: EventMiddleware, Pipeline, ResumableChunkAssembler, BackpressureAsyncIterator
Event parsing: adopt a small schema for normalized events; avoid heavyweight validation libs — use typed dataclasses and simple shape checks to minimize overhead
comments: 2026-02-12 - Liam Chen: Created ticket after spike showing duplicated assembler code across three repos. Spike notes linked in design doc.

2026-02-18 - Aisha Kapoor: Prototype of pipeline available in branch feature/stream-middleware. Basic Event dataclass shape: type, seq, payload, resume_token. Observed case where partial delimiter is split across TCP frames; assembler must handle boundary merging.
2026-02-22 - Marisol Vega (PM): Prioritize clear breakage modes in docs; customers need guidance when resume_token cannot be used (e.g., server GC). Add a fallback strategy in rollout plan.

2026-02-26 - Owen Park (Eng reviewer): Suggested API changes: make BackpressureAsyncIterator an aux object returned by pipeline.open() instead of global state; add explicit .ack() for consumed events to unclog buffer under high-throughput loads.

2026-03-01 - Aisha Kapoor: Implemented retry integration: pipeline now emits special ResumeNeeded event which triggers SDK's stream reconnect path and passes assembler.resume_token. Added property assembler.is_consistent to guard against non-resumable gaps.

2026-03-05 - QA: Added flaky test case where duplicate replay produced repeated function call args; fixed by adding per-event idempotency check in assembler using last_seq_seen map. Integration tests pass locally on Mac/Linux.
2026-03-05 - Documentation owner (Ivy Martins): Draft examples added to docs PR; requested a short how-to on migrating from old iterator API
tests: Unit: assembler handles split frame boundaries, duplicate frames, out-of-order small seq windows
Integration: simulate TCP drop after 120 tokens and verify resume completes with identical final message payload
Load: high-throughput stream with small deltas and consumer-induced backpressure to ensure buffer caps and pause/resume semantics are respected
rollout_plan: Feature-gated rollout: default off. 1) land behind feature flag 'stream_middleware' in canary SDK build, 2) smoke tests with internal teams (console, examples), 3) enable for beta orgs with telemetry, 4) after 2 weeks and zero severity regressions, flip default on and mark old API deprecated with 1 minor-release grace period.
migration_notes: Old consumers using raw byte-level stream parsing should switch to pipeline.open() to get BackpressureAsyncIterator. Add a small adapter function examples/compat_adapter.py to help migration. If a resume_token is missing (server GC), the assembler will raise ResumeNotAvailable — callers should fall back to a full restart and may need to re-send recent context per docs.
